title: Interim study of AI data centre land use
subtitle: Affordable housing RFP at 350 St. Andrew, heritage designations, fire master plan, school-board facility sharing, tower concurrence.
overview: Council directed staff to study land use policies for AI data centres, with a spending cap under $50,000 and a report back in the third quarter of 2027. Staff were also told to bring an interim control by-law to the September 28 meeting that would prohibit such uses while the study runs. The motion passed {{vote:m26}}. It follows a delegation and a petition-related discussion from residents concerned about energy, water, noise and light.

Council also authorized staff to issue a request for proposals for affordable rental housing at 350 St. Andrew Street West, Fergus, and to talk with adjacent property owners. Staff were authorized to issue an RFP for a Community Planning Permit System project, with a council decision point after the first phase. Council approved a reciprocal use agreement with the Upper Grand District School Board for shared facilities, and waived 2026 road closure fees for the Monster March.

Other decisions included heritage designations for three properties, waterworks by-law amendments, a chlorine gas vendor of record and municipal concurrence for a satellite antenna compound on Wellington Road 7. Council received the Fire Master Plan for information, with endorsement expected in late September. The mayor reported after closed session that work is underway on parking and more information is coming soon.

decisions.item: AI data centre study and interim control by-law
decisions.detail: Staff will study land use policies for AI data centres, capped under $50,000, report back in Q3 2027, and prepare an interim control by-law for September 28 {{vote:m26}}.

decisions.item: Affordable housing at 350 St. Andrew Street West
decisions.detail: Staff may issue an RFP for disposition or long-term lease, development and management of the site, and open talks with adjacent property owners.
Staff will issue one RFP for the full project under Option 1, with a mandatory council decision after the phase 1 study.

decisions.item: Reciprocal use agreement with Upper Grand District School Board
decisions.detail: The Managing Director of Community Services may finalize minor amendments and sign the agreement for shared use of township and school facilities.
Council exempted the Monster March from road closure fees for 2026 only, pending a broader fee study.
Council gave municipal concurrence for Shared Tower Inc.'s proposed satellite antenna system and authorized a concurrence letter.
Council authorized amending By-law 2006-080, including connection requirements for new development and decommissioning of private wells.
Brenntag Canada Inc. was authorized as vendor of record for chlorine gas used in drinking water disinfection.

debate: A delegate asked council to pause or ban data centres, citing wildfire smoke, climate emissions, and rapid change to land use and local character, and raised concerns about energy and water demand.

Councillors supporting the data centre motion said municipalities need time to get educated before provincial rules exist, and that not every data centre is the same. The motion's sponsor said the year-long pause would leave later choices to the incoming council.

Staff said they have the planning policy expertise in house but may need outside help on water, power and noise. Council removed the 'staff time' wording from the cost cap so external expertise could be used. Staff also noted an interim control by-law can be appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal.

On the telecom tower, a councillor said the applicant should have reached out to neighbours even though federal rules did not require notice. The applicant said the antennas' height meant no notification was required.

On the Monster March, a delegate said the event is volunteer-run with proceeds donated to local food programs. Staff said there is no legacy-event fee structure yet and a fee study will consider subsidies.
